authors: Celio Boulay, Thomas Moulin, Alexander Chai, wurtylex and contributors (per the git history)
title: Origami formalization, explained
h1: Paper folding in Lean: the seven Huzita–Hatori fold axioms proved as theorems, and Haga's fold for thirds
lead: This project models origami folds as reflections of the real plane and proves all seven Huzita–Hatori axioms as theorems: axioms 5 and 7 with exact conditions, and the cubic-solving axiom 6 (for crossing lines) via the intermediate value theorem. It then proves Haga's theorem: folding a square's corner onto the middle of the opposite edge marks a third. There is no sorry; the only Lean axioms postulate the points (and coordinates) of one generated example, and the headline Haga theorems do not use them. The Lean was not built for this site.
desc: An unofficial plain-English tour of the Lean formalization of Huzita–Hatori origami by Celio Boulay, Thomas Moulin, Alexander Chai, wurtylex and others: lines in canonical form, folds as reflections, all seven fold axioms with sharpness results, and Haga's theorem for folding thirds.
startNote: Start with the objects: Line (why lines are stored in a canonical form), Fold and the reflection f_places_p. Then read the headline Axiom 2, the simplest uniqueness proof, and Axiom 6, where a cubic equation appears. Finish with Haga's first theorem, which uses Axiom 2 to fold a third, and its generalisation.
sizeNote: About 1,250 lines of Lean in 9 files under Origami/lightweight_definitions/ (plus about 175 lines of an unimported paper-folding experiment, not covered).
agentCtx: A Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization of Huzita–Hatori origami: points and canonical lines in the real plane, folds as reflections, the seven fold axioms proved as theorems with sharpness results, Haga's theorem, plus a Python/Rust web tool that turns picked folds into Lean.

gloss.Real.sqrt: Real.sqrt x is the nonnegative square root of x (and 0 for negative x).
gloss.Classical.choose: Classical.choose h picks some witness of an existence proof h, without saying which.
